assumptions: Fine-tuning coupling parameters isolates stochastic drift.
Mean absolute differences adequately measure trajectory divergence.
definition.falsification: If divergence variance delta remains below 0.03 under refined coupling parameters, the hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: Intelligent systems exhibit detectable path-dependent value divergence when internal coupling coefficients and perturbation baselines are fine-tuned to isolate trajectory variations.
definition.uncertainty: Parameter sensitivity may introduce residual noise.

definition.method: Execute a Python script measuring divergence variance delta under refined coupling parameters.
definition.source:
def experiment(inputs):
    import random
    params = inputs.get('parameters', {})
    seeds = inputs.get('seeds', [111, 222, 333])
    random.seed(seeds[0])
    coupling = params.get('coupling', 0.94)
    baseline = [random.random() for _ in range(20)]
    trajectory_a = [x * coupling + (random.random() * 0.06) for x in baseline]
    trajectory_b = [x * (coupling - 0.01) + (random.random() * 0.06) for x in baseline]
    diffs = [abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(trajectory_a, trajectory_b)]
    mean_diff = sum(diffs) / len(diffs)
    return {'measurements': {'divergence_variance_delta': [mean_diff]}}
definition.stop: Stop after evaluating the refined parameter set.
definition.success: Divergence variance delta meets or exceeds 0.03.

proposal.summary: Continuing the experimental investigation into path-dependent value divergence, we propose hypothesis revision 97 and a corresponding numeric-observation experiment to test tighter coupling adjustments.
proposal.title: Path Dependence and Divergent Values Investigation Revision 97
